channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Asian stock markets mirror US tech sell-off, Nikkei plunges over 4%
item.description: Asian stock markets face a sharp sell-off on the last trading day of the week, tracking seeking negative cues from United States (US) equity markets. US technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday as stocks of sophisticated chips extended their losses.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Remains below ascending triangle top near 186.00
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around 185.70 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency cross is holding above both the nine-period and 50-period Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), which reinforces a constructive near-term bias.

item.title: Chinese Yuan loses as safe-haven demand lifts US Dollar
item.description: USD/CNH gains ground for the second successive day, trading around 6.7760 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) receives support from escalating developments surrounding conflicts in the Middle East.

item.title: Japanese Yen softens on renewed US-Iran tensions, Japan flags intervention risk
item.description: The USD/JPY pair posts modest gains near 162.40 during the Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Japanese Yen (JPY) as the United States (US) launches a new wave of strikes against Iran for a sixth night in a row.

item.title: Australian Dollar moves away from three-week top as geopolitics and Fed hike bets lift USD
item.description: The AUD/USD pair remains on the back foot for the second straight day and slides to the 0.7980 region during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: WTI extends range play around $79.00; bullish potential intact amid Mideast tensions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US crude oil price – edges higher during the Asian session on Friday, though it remains confined within a multi-day-old range.

item.title: British Pound weakens below 1.3500 as US launches new wave of strikes against Iran
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades on a softer note around 1.3470 during the Asian trading hours on Friday. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East trigger risk-off market sentiment and weigh on the Cable. The preliminary reading of the Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index for July is due later on Friday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $55.50 amid interest rate concerns
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) remains subdued for the third successive day, trading around $55.50 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Thursday. Silver is on track to drop over 7% this week as escalating Middle East tensions drive oil prices up.

item.title: US President Donald Trump begins widely anticipated address to the nation
item.description: US President Donald Trump is delivering a primetime address to the nation from the White House on Friday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7934 vs. 6.7909 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7934 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7909 and 6.7734 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says ready to act on currency moves whenever necessary
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the authorities are ready to act on currency moves whenever necessary.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises amid sticky inflation fears, escalating Middle East tensions
item.description: NZD/USD inches higher after posting minor losses in the previous day, trading around 0.5840 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency pair remains stronger as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) holds its ground following the release of the country's latest food price data.

item.title: United States Dollar Index consolidates above 100.50 as traders look to Trump's speech
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, is seen oscillating in a narrow range just above the 100.50 level as traders await US President Donald Trump's speech.

item.title: Euro flatlines near 1.1450 amid renewed Hormuz hostilities
item.description: The EUR/USD pair holds steady around 1.1445 during the early Asian session on Friday. Traders continue to digest the developments surrounding the Middle East conflicts. The preliminary reading of the Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index for July will be published later on Friday.

item.title: Iran tells Houthis to close Red Sea oil route if US hits power network — Reuters
item.description: Iran has asked Yemen’s Houthi militia to stand ready to close the Red Sea oil route if the United States (US) strikes Iranian power infrastructure, posing a potent new threat to global energy supplies, Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: Gold tumbles to eight-month low below $4,000 as Middle East tensions reinforce US rate hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) falls to near an eight-month low around $3,975 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal extends its downside as rising tensions in the Middle East raise inflation concerns and reinforce expectations of elevated US interest rates.

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson: Current policy is well positioned to respond, based on incoming data
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said that the current policy stance should support the job market and allow inflation to resume decline toward 2% as tariff effects and energy prices pass through, Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: South Korean Won: BoK hike and semiconductor volatility – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights a hawkish 25bp hike by the Bank of Korea (BoK) to 2.75%, with guidance that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and core inflation will exceed earlier forecasts.

item.title: The Japanese Yen is boxed between a floor it hates and a ceiling nobody trusts
item.description: Dollar-Yen has spent the week doing almost nothing at the most dramatic level in four decades.

item.title: Crude Oil watches the region catch fire and still cannot clear its ceiling
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil is fading about one percent to just below $79.00 after a third consecutive failure at the $80.00 handle, where the 50-day Exponential Moving Average sits just above the figure and refuses to yield.

item.title: The Australian Dollar stalls exactly where everybody said it would
item.description: The Australian Dollar is going nowhere with great precision, with AUD/USD flat on the session and pinned to the 0.7000 handle for a fourth consecutive day.

item.title: The British Pound Sterling gets a new Prime Minister and an old problem
item.description: Sterling is enduring its heaviest session of the month, with GBP/USD fading around half of one percent to just below 1.3500 after the week's advance stalled short of 1.3550 for a second consecutive day.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Retreats from 18-year high, struggles at 220
item.description: The GBP/JPY retreats some 0.34% on Thursday after the pair reached a new 18-year high of 219.62 on Wednesday. Nevertheless, at the time of writing, the cross-pair retreated to 218.80, down 0.34%, as the Yen recovers some ground.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Upside bias toward 6.7600 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that USD/CNH downside momentum continues to build after the pair slipped to 6.7653. Intraday, there is a chance of testing major support at 6.7600 while staying below 6.7780.

item.title: South Korean Won: Hawkish BoK and equity correction support – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the Korean Won (KRW) is outperforming, supported by a hawkish 25 bps Bank of Korea (BoK) hike to 2.75% and expectations that growth and core inflation will exceed 2026 projections.

item.title: Thai Baht: Overvaluation points to weakness against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that softer US inflation data has weakened the Dollar and lowered Fed rate hike expectations, but USD/THB has still broken above 33.50.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Swissie rebounds at 0.8042 support
item.description: The USD/CHF reversed course, rising by over 0.40% late Thursday as the Greenback staged a recovery amid overall risk aversion, heightened tensions in the Middle East, and strong US economic data. The pair trades at 0.8088 after bouncing off daily lows of 0.8045.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rises on resilient labor data, while Oil and Gold fall
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) rises toward 100.80, gaining around 0.3% as stronger-than-expected United States labor-market data supports the Greenback. US Initial Jobless Claims fell to 208K, below expectations of 217K and the previous 216K.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Further upside risk builds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD downside momentum has intensified after a sharp intraday swing, with firm support highlighted at 1.2875 and 1.2860.

item.title: Mexican Peso drops as risk aversion underpins the US Dollar
item.description: The Mexican Peso depreciated by about 0.30% on Thursday as market participants turned risk-averse amid an escalation of the Middle East conflict, which has driven energy prices higher.
